turns.text: Hey, could you pull up the parking permit terms document in my home files? I'm trying to get my condo parking sorted out, so I need you to lay out what the association needs from me before the permit renews and what the renewal actually covers.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
Found it — `documents/home/corvid_court_parking_permit_terms.md`. Here is the full picture.

---

**What the association needs from you before the permit renews**

All five items must reach the office (Suite A) by the **last working day of February** — that's **Friday, February 26** this year. A slip that arrives without any one of them is held, not processed, and they write to you.

| # | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The renewal slip, signed | Mailed to each unit in the second week of February |
| 2 | Vehicle registration and make, written on the slip | If you've changed vehicles, they want a new slip, not an amended one |
| 3 | Current certificate of insurance for that vehicle | A copy, not the original. Watch the expiry date — the office reads it, so if the cert expired between when you copied it and when the slip arrives, it gets held |
| 4 | The permit fee | **$60.00** for the year — same as last year, unchanged since the bays were resurfaced out of the reserve |
| 5 | The old permit card, returned | They will not reissue while the old card is out |

**What the renewal actually covers**

- Your unit's numbered bay — all year
- The two front visitor bays — for a visitor you sign in, up to 48 hours at a time

**What it does not cover**

- A second vehicle
- A trailer
- The loading area at the rear

**A couple of things to keep in mind**

The permit number carries over to the new card, so if you have given that number to a delivery service or your employer, you do not need to give it again. If the permit lapses, you keep the bay, but your vehicle in it without a current permit is treated as a visitor vehicle — the 48-hour limit starts counting from the day the permit lapses.

The renewal slip itself has not gone out yet — they post them in the second week of February, so it should arrive any day now. Want me to flag it when it does, or draft the slip in advance so all you need to do is sign and attach the insurance copy?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Having the downstream lapse rules and the insurance expiration catch laid out right alongside the requirements gives me the exact full picture I needed. Hold off on drafting the slip or setting up any flags for now, I can keep an eye out for the mail myself.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Glad that gave you the whole picture. The February window is straightforward enough that you are not going to trip on anything if you keep the insurance cert date and the old card return in mind when the slip lands. Holler when you need anything else.
